scope: An independently authored fixed-grid body table contains a dedicated bookmark in a cell with four explicit physical margins. A prepared synthetic cross-tab is placed there; this working-tree observation does not establish arbitrary nested-table, native, tagged or live Word compatibility.
schema: Open XML SDK 3.5.1 reported zero errors for the independent explicit-margin input and placed DOCX; validator DLL SHA-256 4126071233c70310683c0fa0b65648bbd34839afa7b0a2309fba13c22501ddec.
independentReader: LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 420(Build:2), Ubuntu 24.04, writer_pdf_Export, pinned Noto fonts, image sha256:a3aaef646226d406fc2b511462beb0359f4cd8859d775f404bd8f137dfd5f644; Poppler 25.03.0 pdftotext -layout and -bbox-layout on the host.
result: The checker found the original outer width/fill and neighboring content, four nested rows with expected decimal totals, a grid within the 3760-twip usable cell width, explicit nested margins and no repeating nested header. Both PDF extractions contained the same table rows. Six selected column origins differed by at most 0.1 points, under the case's 0.2-point check; glyph widths and general page parity are not claimed. The unrelated neighboring cell retained implicit margins and its text origin still differed by 5.5 points.

retainedImplicitMarginFailure.observation: The first prototype admitted missing margins. Its Row origin was 72.0 points in WordNet and 82.9 points in LibreOffice, a 10.9-point difference. The final working-tree profile rejects implicit, partial or ambiguous target margins before reading records and writes explicit nested-cell margins. The discrepancy and its original artifacts remain recorded.

earlierAttempts: The first focused compile found a duplicate local name (CS0136), and the next found a repeated constant array analyzer error (CA1861); both were corrected before the focused runs passed.
limitations: The input generator, probe and checker are committed; generated documents and PDFs remain scratch artifacts. Exact-commit, package and hosted runtime qualification require separate evidence.
